# Open Claude UI source integration

Source: [Caho1/open-claude-ui](https://github.com/Caho1/open-claude-ui), commit `638800b8a4cee4513c8763c3df0ecf8a77b32379`. Copyright 2026 Caho1; MIT license is preserved beside these files.

The files are copied from `code-examples/`. This directory is a deliberate versioned integration boundary: upstream sync updates the reference checkout, and changes here are reviewed with Pilaude's runtime tests before adoption.

Latest checkout audit (2026-10-18): fork `7490e105e418adf2b94c55ff716bb0973d44fb85` contains author main `638800b8a4cee4513c8763c3df0ecf8a77b32379`. The three files below are vendored from that author commit, retaining the documented Button adaptations. Vendoring is distinct from runtime consumption: the theme and data-import Button have consumers; `lib/cds-motion.ts` now imports the solver and actual SNAPPY preset for the placed DOM menu's sampled opacity entry. The library's macOS 2.37337.1 evidence does not establish parity with the selected Windows stable 2.42304.0. See the [33-module and algorithm adoption ledger](../../docs/pilaude-component-adoption.md) for actual consumer evidence and the [visual/interaction parity gates](../../docs/pilaude-ui-parity.md). Full visual/interaction parity has not passed.

| Source | Use in Pilaude | Adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cds-theme.css` | Imported before the existing native theme; supplies CDS light/dark surfaces, clay, dual-ring shadows, radii and keyframes | Trailing whitespace / LF normalization only |
| `CdsButton.tsx` | [PilaudeDataSection](../../components/PilaudeDataSection.tsx) data preview/import actions, mounted by SettingsPanel. The current quiet welcome page uses ordinary buttons, not CdsButton. | Default `type="button"`; adds explicit variant/size classes, styled in `native-theme.css` for Tailwind 4. Dark ink on clay preserves small-text contrast. |
| `ClaudeMotionPresets.ts` | [cds-motion](../../lib/cds-motion.ts) imports `calcDampedHarmonicOscillator` and SNAPPY 320/28/1; [DomContextMenuHost](../../components/DomContextMenuHost.tsx) consumes the 61-point CSS `linear()` curve after placement. | Vendor remains unchanged apart from whitespace normalization. The adapter validates inputs and corrects near-critical/heavy-damping numerical edges. Only opacity enters: no spatial bounce, transform, exit hold or other variants. Reduced motion is static. See the ledger for tests and actual-page evidence. |

System font stacks follow `assets/README.md`; Pilaude loads no font from Google at runtime/build time. The current composer follows the user's later compact reference: 48 CSS px single-line height, 14.4 CSS px radius and a neutral fine border without an outer focus glow. The earlier 20px/dual-ring mapping is historical. The opaque bottom fade is a product adaptation, not consumption of the upstream ScrollFadeContainer sensor.

The 150ms input latch from `useClaudeScrollPinning` is explicitly adapted in [lib/cds-scroll.ts](../../lib/cds-scroll.ts) and consumed by [useAgentSession](../../hooks/useAgentSession.ts), preserving Pi's history restoration and scroll anchors. This records only the latch, not the whole upstream hook. MCP decisions, Cowork, split-pane and keyboard components remain unadopted; similar Pi implementations are independent. Changes consumes attributed table/gutter, roving-index and scroll-edge adaptations. Image geometry is adapted in `lib/image-view-transform.ts` and consumed by ImagePreview for cursor zoom, bounded pan and wheel input; shared-element transitions remain unadopted. Each validation scope and remaining difference is recorded in the adoption ledger. Demo timers, static agents and model data must be replaced by real runtime state before adoption; no UI component supplies an execution permission policy. Windows controls continue to use Tauri's native APIs.

The [ThinkingAccordion.tsx source](https://github.com/Caho1/open-claude-ui/blob/638800b8a4cee4513c8763c3df0ecf8a77b32379/code-examples/ThinkingAccordion.tsx) at the same author commit is adapted outside this vendor directory in [ThinkingDisclosure.tsx](../../components/ThinkingDisclosure.tsx) and [native-theme.css](../../app/native-theme.css), consumed by the real `ThinkingBlock` in [MessageView.tsx](../../components/MessageView.tsx). Only its Grid `0fr`/`1fr`, `min-height: 0` clipping and 200ms `cubic-bezier(.19,1,.22,1)` disclosure mechanism are adapted; the complete source component is not vendored or directly adopted. The source remains Copyright (c) 2026 Caho1, under the adjacent [MIT license](LICENSE).

This controlled adapter preserves Pi's expansion preference and notifications, deferred-history fetch/cache/retry, early-close response isolation, exact source text, existing duration metadata and IME behavior. Native button semantics, linked ARIA region, immediate `inert`/`aria-hidden` on close, content retention until the close transition ends and reduced-motion cleanup are product adaptations. There is no per-block active wire flag, so it adds no active indicator and no forced-live expansion; the source's clipboard action, copy timer, elapsed formatting and simulated timing are not adopted. As of 2026-10-19, 126 affected regression checks and nine actual-page groups have passed, including deferred cache/retry, keyboard/preference changes, motion interruption cleanup and dark/light 390px layout. `ThinkingAccordion` is recorded as **partial adoption of Grid disclosure only**. No matching Windows reference or complete component/visual acceptance is claimed; see the ledger for the final batch evidence.

The latest theme references neutral-surface and fast/slow-duration aliases without defining them. `native-theme.css` supplies those aliases from Pilaude surfaces and the upstream token docs (60ms / 450ms). The variable guard recognizes CSS `@property` registrations used by the new scroll-fade engine. These integrations do not establish Windows motion parity.
